{{Short description|Mathematic theory}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], '''Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology''' is a ''p''-adic [[cohomology theory]] defined for non-singular [[Affine variety|affine varieties]] over [[field (mathematics)|field]]s of positive [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] ''p'' introduced by {{harvs|txt|author1-link=Paul Monsky|last1=Monsky|first1=Paul|last2=Washnitzer|first2=Gerard|author2-link=Gerard Washnitzer|year=1968}}, who were motivated by the work  of {{harvs|txt|last=Dwork|first=Bernard|authorlink=Bernard Dwork|year=1960}}. The idea is to [[lift (mathematics)|lift]] the variety to characteristic 0, and then take a suitable subalgebra of the [[algebraic de Rham cohomology]] of {{harvtxt|Grothendieck|1966}}. The construction was simplified by {{harvtxt|van der Put|1986}}. Its extension to more general varieties is called [[rigid cohomology]].
